transfer.stem: Which summary keeps the instructions and sequence?
transfer.passage:
A call after arrival
Our club received a parcel. It was smaller than I had expected: that compared its size with my expectation, without giving exact measurements. A separate package contained all the parts for a model. Having all the parts did not mean the model had already been assembled.
The office asked us to contact it if our plans changed. The condition did not confirm that our plans had changed. A teacher said, “Please call me when the bus reaches town.” Another pupil wrote, “Give me a ring when you arrive.” Here ring meant a phone call, not a piece of jewellery; neither instruction proved that arrival or a call had already happened.
We were asked to reply before the end of the week. Waiting until next week would miss that boundary. One pupil did not respond until he had checked the facts: checking came first, and there was no earlier response. Later, we had a quick chat beside the school gate. It was brief, and the place was the gate, not the middle of the playground.

options.text: Ring means a phone call; replying next week meets the deadline; he checked the facts before responding.
Ring means a phone call; reply before the week ends; he checked the facts before responding.
Ring means a jewellery gift; reply before the week ends; he checked the facts before responding.
Ring means a phone call; reply before the week ends; he responded before checking the facts.

answer.display: Ring means a phone call; reply before the week ends; he checked the facts before responding.
